page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, this instance configures 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The host provides 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 16 MB of L3 cache and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Local disk storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring attached block storage for boot and persistent volume needs. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, FMA, and BMI2 hardware acceleration.

Performance evaluations reflect average capabilities for single-threaded tasks alongside weak multi-core throughput scaling. The instance records a stress-ng single-core score of 767.9 and multi-core score of 1535.77. Single-threaded benchmarks perform reliably, achieving a gzip compression throughput of 23.96 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0. Conversely, multi-threaded operations like bzip3 decompression (18.36 GB/sec), Geekbench software compilation (3778.0), and Redis SET operations (3.57 million ops/sec) score lower within comparative benchmarks. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 31.36 GB/sec for reads and 16.16 GB/sec for writes across large blocks.

Featuring a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU core allocations, ecs.c6a.xlarge offers a entry-level compute profile that eliminates vCPU credit throttling risks associated with burstable classes. The hardware design is cost-efficient for small-scale microservices, code compilation test environments, utility scripts, and basic static web applications. The primary trade-offs include memory capacity constraints and reduced multi-threaded efficiency under heavy concurrent processing loads.
